variants.context: Image captioning turns visual evidence into a natural-language description. A captioning system first represents image regions or patches, then a language decoder generates words that describe objects, attributes, actions, text, and relationships.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Accessibility
pairs.detail: Describe the information or function a person needs in the surrounding page.
pairs.explanation: Describe the information or function a person needs in the surrounding page. Decorative images may need empty alternative text; complex charts may need a longer structured description.

pairs.label: Search metadata
pairs.detail: Prefer grounded objects, attributes, relationships, and OCR fields that improve retrieval.
pairs.explanation: Prefer grounded objects, attributes, relationships, and OCR fields that improve retrieval. Structured claims may be more useful than one polished sentence.

pairs.label: Editorial draft
pairs.detail: Offer an editable proposal with explicit user control.
pairs.explanation: Offer an editable proposal with explicit user control. Tone can vary, but invented names, identities, events, and sensitive traits remain disallowed.

pairs.label: Specialist workflow
pairs.detail: Route medical, legal, safety-critical, biometric, and other high-impact imagery to domain policy and qualified human review.
pairs.explanation: Route medical, legal, safety-critical, biometric, and other high-impact imagery to domain policy and qualified human review.

pairs.label: Greedy
pairs.detail: Choose the highest-probability token at every step.
pairs.explanation: Choose the highest-probability token at every step. It is fast and deterministic, but an early local choice can block a better complete caption.

pairs.label: Beam search
pairs.detail: Keep multiple partial sequences and compare their accumulated scores.
pairs.explanation: Keep multiple partial sequences and compare their accumulated scores. Wider search costs more decoder work and can favor generic, fluent language priors.

pairs.label: Sampling
pairs.detail: Sample from a temperature- or probability-filtered distribution.
pairs.explanation: Sample from a temperature- or probability-filtered distribution. It can improve variety for editorial drafts but needs stronger grounding and reproducibility controls.

pairs.label: Qualify offline
pairs.detail: Pass data-lineage, deterministic, hallucination, accessibility, safety, privacy, slice, latency, and failover tests on the complete artifact bundle.
pairs.explanation: Pass data-lineage, deterministic, hallucination, accessibility, safety, privacy, slice, latency, and failover tests on the complete artifact bundle.

pairs.label: Observe in shadow
pairs.detail: Run production-shaped traffic without returning candidate captions.
pairs.explanation: Run production-shaped traffic without returning candidate captions. Verify routing, telemetry, capacity, and disagreement against the current system.

pairs.label: Canary by route
pairs.detail: Assign stable cohorts and keep exposure within a pre-approved blast radius.
pairs.explanation: Assign stable cohorts and keep exposure within a pre-approved blast radius. Watch hard gates and the specific user consequence each route creates.

pairs.label: Expand or reverse
pairs.detail: Increase exposure only while every required gate remains healthy.
pairs.explanation: Increase exposure only while every required gate remains healthy. Roll back the model-policy bundle when evidence fails or becomes unavailable.

variants.prompt: What is the core invariant of a grounded image-captioning system?
options: The decoder must always return the longest fluent sentence.
Every factual claim in a released caption must be supported by permitted image or context evidence.
A high CIDEr score is enough to release a caption.
Beam search must use at least five candidates.
variants.explanation: Fluency and reference similarity do not establish factual support. Claims need traceable evidence or the system should omit, hedge, review, or abstain.

variants.prompt: Which data practice best protects evaluation integrity?
options: Use the same near-duplicate images in training and the release set.
Accept synthetic captions as trusted labels without provenance.
Tune thresholds repeatedly on the final release set.
Split by image lineage, deduplicate across splits, and keep a versioned frozen release set.

variants.prompt: What is the safest behavior when the required grounding service is unavailable?
options: Bypass grounding to preserve caption coverage.
Return a previously generated caption from another image.
Increase beam width until one caption looks trustworthy.
Fail closed for automatic release, then use an approved fallback, review queue, or no caption.
